editorNote: Alibaba led the watchlist after unveiling its biggest AI model yet, and Alphabet clawed back its post-earnings selloff on an analyst defense of its capex plan. In crypto, Strategy kept trimming its bitcoin stack to fund buybacks while the Coldcard wallet exploit grew well past its weekend total. Gold ticked between gains and losses as a paused Iran airstrike briefly drained its war premium.

stories.headline: Alibaba unveils 2.4-trillion-parameter Qwen3.8-Max, shares jump as much as 7%
stories.summary: Alibaba introduced Qwen3.8-Max, a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 2.4 trillion total parameters (95 billion active) and a 1-million-token context window, saying it beat rival Moonshot's Kimi K3 on several coding and multimodal benchmarks while trailing on some general reasoning tests. Alibaba's Hong Kong shares closed 7% higher and its U.S. ADRs rose 4.5% in premarket trading; the company plans to open-source the model's weights next week, its first time doing so at this scale.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the first Max-class Qwen model Alibaba has open-sourced, a move that pressures rival Chinese labs on price and narrows the gap analysts estimate between Chinese and U.S. frontier models to three to six months.

sourceLinks.title: Forbes: Alibaba Unveils Its Largest AI Model Yet As China Closes The Gap

stories.headline: Alphabet shares jump 5% as Morgan Stanley defends its AI capex
stories.summary: Alphabet stock rose 5.1% Monday after Morgan Stanley analysts told clients the company's raised 2026 capex forecast of $195-205 billion is justified, pointing to $53.3 billion in trailing-12-month free cash flow and financing options including leasing and custom chips. The move reverses a slide that had kept Alphabet below its pre-earnings price all last week, after strong Q2 results (EPS of $9.11, triple estimates) were overshadowed by the higher spending forecast.
stories.whyItMatters: The rally shows investor anxiety over Alphabet's AI spending was more about financing-plan clarity than about the size of the number itself.

sourceLinks.title: The Motley Fool: Why Alphabet Stock Popped Today

stories.headline: Coldcard hack losses climb past $100M as a fourth wave hits
stories.summary: The Coldcard hardware-wallet exploit has now drained a confirmed 1,596 BTC (over $100M) from roughly 7,300 addresses across three confirmed waves and 14 smaller incidents, up sharply from the ~$89M and 4,585 addresses reported over the weekend. A suspected fourth wave was detected live on August 3, moving about 449 BTC across 218 transactions in 2.5 hours; Coinkite has shipped emergency firmware updates and destroyed its remaining vulnerable inventory.
stories.whyItMatters: The new wave shows the exploit isn't slowing down even after vendor remediation, and Galaxy Research is now advising anyone on the affected firmware to treat their wallet as compromised.

sourceLinks.title: CryptoTimes: Coldcard Hack Losses Hit $100M With 1,596 BTC Stolen

stories.headline: Strategy sells another 1,638 bitcoin to fund STRC buybacks and cash reserve
stories.summary: Strategy sold 1,638 BTC for $104.7 million and raised $290.6 million issuing common shares, using the combined $395 million to repurchase 912,143 STRC preferred shares for $81.2 million, fund preferred dividends, and add $250 million to its cash reserve, now at $4 billion. The sale trims Strategy's bitcoin holdings to 842,138 BTC.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a continuation of Strategy's shift away from pure accumulation toward managing its capital structure with periodic bitcoin sales.

sourceLinks.title: CoinDesk: Strategy sold another $105 million of bitcoin last week, repurchased $81.2 million of STRC

stories.headline: Gold slips toward $4,071 as a paused Iran airstrike eases the war premium
stories.summary: Gold futures opened 0.7% higher at $4,135.20 on Monday after President Trump said the U.S. would pause planned airstrikes on Iran, but prices retreated through the day to around $4,071-4,111 as Iran said it was not directly negotiating with Washington, only discussing the Strait of Hormuz with Oman.
stories.whyItMatters: The pullback shows gold's recent strength has leaned heavily on geopolitical risk premium, which can unwind quickly once tensions ease even briefly.

sourceLinks.title: Yahoo Finance: Gold prices today, Monday, August 3, 2026
